project: NAS File Browser + YouTube Audio Downloader
description: A lightweight personal NAS file browser with integrated YouTube audio download, auto-conversion, and auto-split capabilities. Built with Python/FastAPI/Jinja2/HTMX/SQLite/yt-dlp/ffmpeg/Docker.

userStories.title: Project scaffolding, database schema, and basic layout
userStories.description: As a developer, I want the project initialized with FastAPI/Jinja2/HTMX/SQLite, database schema created, and a basic dark-theme three-column layout shell (tree sidebar, file list main area, player panel) so that all subsequent features have a foundation to build on.
acceptanceCriteria: Initialize FastAPI project with Jinja2 templates and HTMX
Create SQLite database with tables for config, download_history, and file_metadata
Implement basic module structure (file management, YouTube download, audio processing, config)
Render a basic layout with left directory tree sidebar, center file list area, and right player panel (collapsed by default)
Dark theme applied as default
Typecheck passes

userStories.title: Config management backend and UI with dependency detection
userStories.description: As a user, I want to configure the NAS root directory and file deletion strategy through a Web UI, and I want the system to auto-detect yt-dlp and ffmpeg on startup so that I can set up the tool without touching config files.
acceptanceCriteria: Backend routes for reading and updating system config in SQLite
Auto-detect yt-dlp and ffmpeg installation on startup, store status in config
Web UI page to set NAS root directory path
Web UI page to choose file deletion strategy (recycle bin or direct delete)
Display dependency status (yt-dlp installed/missing, ffmpeg installed/missing)
Typecheck passes

userStories.title: Directory tree navigation
userStories.description: As a user, I want a directory tree in the left sidebar showing the NAS directory structure, so that I can quickly navigate to any target folder.
acceptanceCriteria: Display NAS root directory and subdirectories as a tree in the left sidebar
Support expand/collapse of directory nodes via HTMX
Click a directory to select it and update the file list
Show current selected directory highlighted
Support returning to parent directory
Typecheck passes
Verify in browser

userStories.title: File list display
userStories.description: As a user, I want to see a file list in the main area showing filename, size, modified time, and type with icons, so that I can understand the contents of the current directory.
acceptanceCriteria: Display file list with columns: filename, size, modified time, file type
Show file type icons (folder, audio, generic file)
Double-click a folder to navigate into it
Display breadcrumb or path indicator for current directory
Return to parent directory via button
Typecheck passes
Verify in browser

userStories.title: File search and sorting
userStories.description: As a user, I want to search files by name and sort the file list by different fields, so that I can quickly find and organize files.
acceptanceCriteria: Search input that filters files by name in the current directory
Sort dropdown/buttons supporting sort by name, size, modified time, type
Sorting toggles between ascending and descending
Search and sort update the file list via HTMX without full page reload
Typecheck passes
Verify in browser

userStories.title: File operations (create, rename, delete, move)
userStories.description: As a user, I want to create new folders, rename files, delete files, and move files, so that I can manage and organize my files directly in the browser.
acceptanceCriteria: Create new folder button that prompts for name and creates directory
Rename file/folder via context menu or inline edit
Delete file/folder with confirmation dialog; behavior matches configured deletion strategy (recycle bin or direct delete)
Move file/folder via drag-and-drop or cut/paste
All file operations update the file list via HTMX
Typecheck passes
Verify in browser

userStories.title: Download bar with URL input, format selection, and split options
userStories.description: As a user, I want a fixed download bar at the top of the page where I can paste a YouTube URL, select audio format, and configure auto-split options, so that I can start a download from any view.
acceptanceCriteria: Fixed download bar at the top of the page, always visible
YouTube URL input field with validation (YouTube URLs only)
Audio format dropdown with options: MP3, M4A, FLAC
Auto-split toggle checkbox to enable/disable song splitting
Split mode selector (chapter info / silence detection) shown when auto-split is enabled
Keep original file checkbox shown when auto-split is enabled
Save location defaults to current browsed directory
Typecheck passes
Verify in browser

userStories.title: Video info fetching and download preview
userStories.description: As a user, I want the system to automatically fetch video information (cover image, title, duration) when I paste a YouTube URL, so that I can confirm the correct video before downloading.
acceptanceCriteria: Auto-fetch video metadata (title, thumbnail, duration) after valid YouTube URL is entered
Display preview card with video title, thumbnail, and duration
Show confirm/download button on the preview card
Handle invalid URLs or unavailable videos with error message
Typecheck passes
Verify in browser
userStories.notes: Implemented with yt-dlp backend endpoint, auto-fetch on valid URL input, preview card with thumbnail/title/uploader/views/duration, error handling for invalid/unavailable videos

userStories.title: Download execution with real-time progress and queue
userStories.description: As a user, I want to start downloads and see real-time progress, with support for multiple queued tasks, so that I can monitor and batch-download audio files.
acceptanceCriteria: Backend: yt-dlp download and ffmpeg audio conversion pipeline
Real-time progress bar showing download percentage, current file, and estimated time remaining
Progress updates pushed via WebSocket or SSE
Support multiple concurrent download tasks in a queue
Download complete triggers automatic file list refresh
Typecheck passes
Verify in browser
userStories.notes: Implemented download manager with WebSocket real-time progress, concurrent task queue (max 3), yt-dlp download with ffmpeg conversion, progress bar UI, auto-refresh file list on completion

userStories.title: Audio auto-split for compilations
userStories.description: As a user, I want the system to automatically split downloaded audio compilations into individual tracks using chapter info or silence detection, so that I get properly separated songs.
acceptanceCriteria: After download, analyze chapter metadata if split mode is 'chapter info'
Perform silence detection if split mode is 'silence detection'
Split audio file into individual tracks based on detected boundaries
Rename split files using chapter titles when available
Option to keep or discard the original unsplit file
Split files appear in the current directory after processing
Typecheck passes
Verify in browser
userStories.notes: Implemented audio splitter with chapter info and silence detection using ffmpeg, integrated into download manager with real-time progress UI

userStories.title: Lightweight audio player
userStories.description: As a user, I want a lightweight audio player that appears when I click an audio file, so that I can preview downloaded audio without leaving the file browser.
acceptanceCriteria: Click an audio file to open a lightweight player in the right panel
Play/pause toggle control
Progress bar with scrub/drag to seek
Display current time and total duration
Player stays open while browsing other files
Typecheck passes
Verify in browser
userStories.notes: Implemented audio player with click-to-play, play/pause toggle, progress bar with scrub/drag, time display, and HTMX integration. Player panel expands when audio file is clicked and stays open while browsing.

userStories.title: Responsive design and final polish
userStories.description: As a user, I want the application to work well on different screen sizes with a polished dark-theme interface, so that I can use it from both desktop and mobile devices.
acceptanceCriteria: Responsive layout adapts to different screen widths
Mobile view stacks panels vertically or provides toggle navigation
Dark theme consistently applied across all components
Consistent spacing, typography, and iconography
Basic mobile usability for core file browsing features
Typecheck passes
Verify in browser
userStories.notes: Implemented responsive design with CSS media queries for mobile and tablet, added mobile menu toggle and player toggle buttons, touch-friendly improvements, dark theme consistency, and accessibility features
